reports.desc: received an email evite through Greetings Island and asked to log in to open by supplying email and password.

No way, I blocked the "tips@bayareatimes.com" email address associated with Bay Area Times. A few minutes ago, they sent an email using "growth@bayareatimes.com". I had flagged these messages as spam or phishing attempts and warned my family against clicking any links inside them. Now, this scam operation used the rolling email address tactic where their active email address changes automatically at set intervals or per interaction, similar to a rotating IP address.

I received a call on October 14, 2026 from a "Service Activation Center" regarding extended warranty related to the vehicle I'm currently financing. They made it sound like they were a third-party company working with Volkswagen, the make of car I'm currently financing. Its my first time financing a car and they had all information regarding my vehicle so I had thought it was legitimate. Due to my believing they were legitimate, I gave them my bank account information as they "require: it to make the monthly payments. However, after looking into it further, I realized multiple other people have been subject to the same scam and want to make sure as much people are aware of it as possible.
